findings.reason: Confirmed as a proof/supplier gap, not a counterexample to affineness. I read §§2.2–2.3 and pp. 38–46, inspecting pp. 19, 44–45 as images. With principal polarizations and one common G-similitude scalar, an honest isogeny invertible on a nonzero étale part has unit scalar; duality and the polarization degree identity then force it to be an isomorphism. Footnote 15 treats the outer parts separately and does not establish compatibility with that scalar. The word vacuous needs this nonzero-étale qualification. Replacing isogeny by quasi-isogeny alone is not a proof: the kernel construction and compactified transport must be established for the replacement. Record the gap under §18 and keep those proof gates explicit in IG.1–2.

Confirmed. The standing choice in §2.5.7, p. 27 requires the prime-to-q part of N to be at least 3 for each relevant good prime q. Item 21 reproduces the toroidal theorem without that ambient level condition. Restore the standing condition, together with the fan/base hypotheses, in the extraction and the compactification application; do not infer it merely from N ≥ 3.

Confirmed with scope qualification. §§2.8 and 5.1, pp. 35–36 and 64–65 specify F0, splitness in F0, the character varpi, its ramification in S and the sufficiently divisible prime-to-p level N0. Items 31–32 suppress part of this data. IG.5 gives the totally split residual obstruction, while the rational existence theorem uses the wider F0-split setting. State each branch separately, retain all hypotheses and request the wider application where needed; a specialization is still a valid planned result.

Confirmed only for the unrecorded descent steps. Lemma 2.1.1, p. 12 already covers general neat compact open K, so the finding is wrong to restrict that lemma to principal congruence level. The final argument on p. 36 proves vanishing using the auxiliary principal prime-to-p level and enlarged bad-place set. Record the Hecke-equivariant level/descent and Hecke-algebra contraction needed to recover the stated general level. Use the all-N good-reduction comparison of Proposition 2.6.4 when p-power level is present. This is not evidence that Theorem 1.1 is false.

Confirmed. The ambient flag description in §§2.6–2.7 must specify the Hodge cocharacter and the dimension of the isotropic subspace, not all isotropic subspaces of arbitrary rank. For this datum the rank is n at every embedding, and d=[F+:Q]n². Item 24 and IG.3 should expose that type and its polarization/endomorphism conditions. The intended flag variety is recoverable from the setup; the correction makes the definition usable rather than disproving the theorem.

Confirmed. The proof of Proposition 2.2.4, pp. 16–17 uses bounded quasi-isogeny representatives and a finite truncation detecting the relevant p-divisible-group condition, with the cited Rapoport–Zink/Oort inputs. The extraction leaves those results inside a proof note. IG.0 has an effectivity target, but that does not identify these particular theorem interfaces. Add individual cited-input records and requests to the existing p-divisible/moduli suppliers, with the actual bounds and hypotheses, before crediting the application.

Confirmed. Propositions 3.3.4 and 3.3.8, pp. 46–50 distinguish the integral affine pro-Igusa normalization from its finite-level versions. Item 43 calls the general pro-cover finite; finiteness is only justified at the appropriate finite level, whereas integrality survives the limit. Separate the finite and perfect/pro-level statements and notation. The affinoid assertion on p. 59 also cites 3.3.8 where the argument needs the preceding affineness and integral normalization results. Preserve the correct integral statement rather than replacing it by a blanket non-finiteness assertion in degenerate finite cases.

Confirmed as an explicit finite-level target omission. §§3.2–3.3 include finite-level toroidal existence, formal charts and boundary descriptions in Theorems 3.2.4, 3.2.6, 3.3.12 and 3.3.15, in addition to their perfect limits. The extraction records them, but IG.2 does not specify the full finite-level package and compatibility maps. Expand its packet targets or requests before treating every one as covered. IG.1 already plans the finite-level open Igusa tower and must remain its owner.

Confirmed. I read Theorem 4.2.1 and Corollary 4.2.2, pp. 52–53 against item 48 and IG.3. The boundary Hodge–Tate filtration is an explicit formula involving the multiplicative, abelian and étale pieces; merely identifying fibers does not state it. Add that formula, the isotropic filtration, rank/type and equivariance as an application of the common period-map supplier. Assign the common construction once and have IG.3 import it.

Confirmed, with the proposed routes reconciled. The setup of Theorem 4.1.1, Proposition 4.3.1 and Theorem 4.4.1 use SW13 Theorems A/B, not just a Hodge–Tate exact sequence. T2 currently plans the latter, and IG.3 applies classification without supplying it. The SW20 /100–101 route is the proposed prismatic Dieudonné extension; CS17 /53 is missing and suggests T2. Add the omitted cited inputs and choose one supplier with a PEL action/polarization adapter. Do not implement the classification independently in both directions. The rational crystalline full-faithfulness and integral classification statements must remain distinct.

Confirmed. Item 35 lists Lan–Stroh Theorem 2.3.3, whereas the construction and proofs in §3 also invoke Theorem 2.3.2, including its boundary-completion and proper-map package (p. 41). Read against the §3 construction, this is an omitted cited input, not an assertion that nothing whatsoever is planned in IG.2. Add the specific theorem and its well-positioned/fan hypotheses, then request or build its compactification specialization at the existing owner.

Confirmed. The page-66 image really prints rho_m = rho_(m-dual)|Art_F^(-1)|^(1-2n) without contragredience. The published ACC+ duality formulas, pp. 931–932, invert the roots; the correction therefore requires the dual representation as well as the displayed character twist. Without the dual it does not recover the specified Hecke polynomial. IG.5 already states the corrected dualization and eigenvalue dictionary. Record the source slip and cite/import that existing corrected application rather than constructing it again.

Confirmed. Theorem 6.4.1, pp. 84–87 has a Galois-existence assertion as well as the length obstruction. Its last case uses concentration and the rational result of §5. Current IG.6 describes the boundary formula and length conclusion but omits the existence theorem and has no direct or transitive dependency from IG.4 or IG.5. On the assembled 2,956-stage graph, adding those dependencies creates no reverse-path cycle. Add both theorem parts and a uniform lower-rank induction with the classical GL_r torsion input; do not mistake lower-rank boundary factorization alone for the missing last case.

Confirmed. Item 56 does not expose all standing §5.1 hypotheses of Theorem 5.1.2: F+ ≠ Q, the proper imaginary quadratic subfield, splitness of p, varpi and its ramification, S and the sufficiently small tame level. These occur explicitly on pp. 64–66 and matter to the transfer and Galois construction. Restore them and distinguish the totally split mod-ell ordinary obstruction from the wider rational theorem.

Rejected as the asserted missing twisted-source/proof gap. Arthur I §1, p. 327 explicitly works with a connected component of a possibly disconnected reductive group and gives cyclic examples; Arthur II §1, pp. 503–505 retains this setup and states its restriction to the connected or cyclic restriction-of-scalars component form. Thus the claim that these papers treat only connected reductive groups is false. CSnc pp. 72–74 explains the further cuspidality simplification, and current ET.4 explicitly imports the archived Arthur input through AS.6. Making the cited identity and its component hypotheses a separate extraction record would improve granularity, but the proposed new-source proof gap and mandatory replacement references are not established.

Confirmed. The Red^b construction, its dual trace identity and the local nontransfer obstruction are used on pp. 65–67 and 75–78 but are compressed into notes. ET.6 explicitly owns classical GL_m/inner-form comparison, and ET.7b owns the rational Igusa trace specialization. Add separate cited-result interfaces and import these owners, retaining Grothendieck-group signs, virtual multiplicities and all normalization conventions. The semisimple parameter assignment alone cannot supply the nontransfer theorem.

Confirmed. The actual uses of Labesse 1991 at infinity, Labesse 1999 for inverse transfer, Shin 2009 for acceptability/removal, and Hamacher 2019 for non-finite-type compact support appear on pp. 70–76 and 79. The extraction prerequisite list omits them. Add references and precise use/owner notes. This confirms a missing prerequisite ledger, not independent verification of every theorem in those additional papers.

Confirmed with a correction to the compound claim. The proof of Proposition 2.1.2 on p. 12 asserts H¹(Q,Gder)=0; simply connectedness does not kill the real-place classes. For SU(2,2), the determinant-compatible signatures (4,0), (2,2), (0,4) already refute the blanket assertion. The finding itself gives conflicting general counts; do not propagate its universal n+1 formula. The needed input is the locally trivial kernel/Hasse principle plus the precise twisting/torus reduction, not vanishing of all H¹. PEL M3 is the component-comparison owner and needs an explicit supplier/request. Record the false proof step without declaring the proposition false or treating an unverified ker¹ bijection as proved.

Confirmed for source registration and reconciliation, not for alleged automatic invalidity of planned status. The extraction has 52 items with an IG stage in planned, while its original review says 55; its sole source route names BG2–BG3. make_queue.py registers accepted source routes, so the detailed IG obligations are not passed through that route mechanism. Add/reconcile an IG source route and the missing requests and proof gates. Protocol permits planning through reviewed stage prose; absence of a finished blueprint by itself neither makes the status circular nor forces all 52 items to missing.

Add the precise flag-stratum supplier/adapter and required imports; generic BunG stratification is not the whole statement of CSnc Theorem 2.7.3.

BG1 owns the B(G) order/classification and ordinary criterion; the PEL ordinary/central-leaf application also needs its own supplier. Reconcile the existing CS17 and other paper routes before adding one exact adapter/import to IG.3–4. The proposed BG3 imports introduce no cycle in the checked graph.

Confirmed as a hypothesis/source gap. Theorem 5.7.1 prints any place q on p. 77, but the inspected Caraiani theorem has p ≠ ell (arXiv 1010.2188v1, Theorem 1.1, pp. 1–2); CS17 also separates the coefficient-prime comparison. The references quoted here do not by themselves justify that stronger every-place wording. Restrict the recorded theorem to finite q not dividing ell, which includes the needed auxiliary p, or give an additional precise ell-adic theorem with all hypotheses. AG2.5 is the ramified local-global owner; ET.7a also needs the residual-spectrum classification input. Do not present the restricted check as disproving all stronger results in the literature.

Confirmed with normalization corrected exactly once. I compared CSnc pp. 74–77 with CS17 pp. 739–742 and Shin §5.5–5.6: Shin distinguishes n-Red (the normalized composite) from Red=n-Red tensor the half-modulus character, and Lemma 5.10 evaluates the latter at the original test function. Either twist the representation or multiply the test function, not both. The infinity functions on CSnc pp. 74–75 and Shin (6.7) use Xi(phi), so the trivial-coefficient parenthesis is unjustified for proper endoscopic terms (e.g. the 2+2 partition in rank four). Record both inherited discrepancies; rederive the local normalization and retain virtual constituents rather than claiming literal equality pi_j=Red(pi).
